title: C.E.L.L. (Cross Emulation Library Layer)
description: Every language has a unique API to draw images, play sounds, manage files, store arrays, and handle input. However, most languages share a C-like syntax. descriptionHtml:
Every language has a unique API to draw images, play sounds, manage files, store arrays, and handle input. However, most languages share a C-like syntax. By building a native layer per platform, I could create a common UI engine (MicroGen) above any C-like language. Using the MicroGen engine, I proceeded to construct a game engine (PlatformerLib) with physics, common AI, collision, and scripting abilities.

To create a game, the developer has four choices:
  • Start coding above the PlatformerLib layer beginning with a skeleton template.
  • Create scripts for graphic layers, mobs, player, and game events.
  • Use the GUI editor to build the game like Unity.
  • Use a combination of any of the choices above.

I wrote an article for the Software Developer Journal explaining the entire engine and how I made C# syntax compatible with Java.

historicalNotes: The original portfolio described Java and C# syntax compatibility.
